Supplied metadata for /mcp: HTTP 401; Bearer realm OAuth; resource metadata at https://mcp.asana.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource. That document reports resource https://mcp.asana.com, authorization server https://mcp.asana.com, `scopes_supported: ["default"]`, bearer method `header`, and resource name `Asana MCP`. Authorization-server metadata reports code response, authorization_code and refresh_token grants, token auth methods client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, none, PKCE plain and S256, and registration endpoint https://mcp.asana.com/register. V2 docs instead say clients must pre-register and dynamic registration is unsupported. The supplied metadata is for the input /mcp path, while the docs describe /v2/mcp.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic:
1. The official V2 list divides tools into read, write, and interactive categories; it does not publish readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, or openWorldHint annotations. `delete_task` is described as permanent and irreversible.
2. Interactive preview tools render a confirmation UI in Claude and ChatGPT; standard write tools act immediately. The docs say other MCP clients use standard write tools directly, so confirmation is not generally server-enforced.
3. V2 access follows the authenticated user's Asana permissions; sessions are scoped to one selected workspace. App pre-registration and optional workspace distribution apply. Enterprise+ and Legacy Enterprise admins can allow or block specific clients. Docs say one-hour access tokens; supplied /mcp metadata separately advertises DCR and `default` scope.
4. No read-only mode or toolset/filter URL parameter is documented. V2 is workspace-scoped; a separate Command endpoint has a different tool set. The V1 /sse endpoint is deprecated.
5. No MCP-specific PII masking or field redaction is documented. User access boundaries and workspace scope are documented; `get_attachments` returns file names and URLs.
6. `create_tasks` and `update_tasks` support up to 50 tasks per call. `search_tasks` is Premium-only. Other MCP-specific rate, quota, result-truncation, or cost-per-call limits were not found.
7. The docs direct clients to tools/list for current schemas but do not document unknown-argument rejection, coercion, or automatic correction. Tool-specific required filters are described for some tools.
8. MCP-specific logging, audit attribution, telemetry, and opt-out behavior were not found. The general privacy statement describes broader Asana information processing but not MCP call logging.
9. No dedicated vendor rating, reporting, or survey tool was found in the reviewed lists. `add_comment` is for task discussion/context, not vendor feedback.
10. No server-delivered skill tool or initialize instructions were found. Tool descriptions include behavioral guidance; the reference says `get_status_overview` handles its search internally and should not be preceded by other search tools. Such text is client guidance; server enforcement is not documented.
11. No MCP memory feature is documented. Session workspace selection fixes the workspace context for that session.
12. The documented Asana V2 server is a flat tool set; the separate Command server is a distinct endpoint with a different tool set. No nested server proxy is documented.
13. No raw API request, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or equivalent unrestricted tool appears in the official V2 list.

It does not state a numeric total. This yields 27 official actions. Added 10 catalogue-only names from Agent Discoverability's ChatGPT integration listing (2026-10): eight deprecated connector/widget helpers and two versioned preview-tool names. E_aggregated.token_method: No public server code or verbatim complete tools/list output and initialize instructions were available; the official reference points clients to tools/list for current schemas.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The MCP reference documents a selected tool set, while Asana publishes a separate REST API reference with endpoints not represented by dedicated MCP tools, including direct operations for workspaces, custom fields, webhooks, memberships, sections, and other resource types. The MCP tools reference specifically says there is no dedicated V2 goals tool; search_objects can search goals, but the listed MCP tools do not document goal creation or updates.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The docs recommend using tools/list for current schemas and suggest preview tools when users want review before a change. Confirmation is available through interactive UIs in Claude and ChatGPT; standard write calls are used directly by other MCP clients. Guidance in tool descriptions is not shown to be server-enforced.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Asana says MCP access is user-based and actions appear as the authorizing user; the token grants no permissions beyond that user's existing Asana access. V2 access is scoped to one selected workspace. MCP app tokens are separate from API tokens. The privacy statement describes general Asana data processing, but the reviewed pages do not make MCP-specific retention, training, or logging commitments.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Asana describes V2 as generally available, supports Streamable HTTP, and says app management lets eligible organizations allow or block specific clients.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Workspace selection and user permissions are documented access boundaries. Confirmation is limited to client-rendered interactive tools and does not protect ordinary writes across clients. MCP-specific logging, retention, PII masking, telemetry, and training controls were not found in the reviewed documentation.

contradictions: The input endpoint is https://mcp.asana.com/mcp, while Asana's current MCP guide documents https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp. The input path returned HTTP 401 and has its own supplied OAuth metadata, but no tool list was available for that path; actions therefore use the documented V2 list as best available evidence.

Supplied OAuth metadata for /mcp advertises https://mcp.asana.com/register and `scopes_supported: ["default"]`; V2 documentation says clients must pre-register and dynamic client registration is not supported, and says MCP apps do not require specific scopes.

Agent Discoverability reports 35 ChatGPT integration tools and lists versioned preview names plus eight deprecated/internal widget tools not in the official 27-tool reference. Their availability on the remote V2 endpoint is unconfirmed; they are marked third-party in actions.json.
The Claude connector directory lists 15 tools, a subset of the official 27-tool list, and describes the connector as having “30+ tools.” HookMCP reports 27 tools matching the official list.
observations_for_research: Asana's V2 documentation distinguishes immediate write tools from client-rendered preview tools; confirmation coverage depends on the MCP client.
V2 authorization binds a session to one selected workspace, described by Asana as reducing workspace lookup calls and creating a security boundary.
The documented V2 tool set uses consolidated plural names for bulk task creation and updates, while the historical V1 changelog discussion shows earlier tools with different names.
